title: Causal Asymmetry Of Classical And Quantum Autonomous Agents
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 01 September 2026;
tldr: The paper investigates causal asymmetry in classical and quantum autonomous agents and its consequences for information-to-work conversion.
motivation: Autonomous agents, such as Maxwell's demons, are central to information thermodynamics, but how causal structure and quantum effects limit or enable their thermodynamic performance remains an open question.
method: The authors introduce a framework to quantify causal asymmetry for classical and quantum autonomous agents, deriving bounds on work extraction and information processing.
result: They show that quantum agents can exhibit different causal asymmetry than classical ones, potentially allowing thermodynamic advantages or tighter constraints.
conclusion: Causal asymmetry is a fundamental feature of autonomous agents that connects quantum information, causality, and thermodynamics.

title: Superfluid Helium Thin Films As Quantum Field Theory Simulators For Probing Information Area Laws
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 15 September 2026;
tldr: The paper proposes using superfluid helium thin films as analog quantum simulators for quantum field theories to experimentally probe entanglement area laws.
motivation: Area laws of entanglement are fundamental to quantum information but challenging to test in quantum field theories; superfluid helium thin films provide a tunable platform for such simulations.
method: Thin films of superfluid helium are employed to emulate quantum field theory and measure entanglement entropy scaling.
conclusion: This approach offers a promising route to experimentally study entanglement in quantum field theories using condensed matter systems.

title: Single-operation Rydberg Phase Gates Via Dynamic Population Suppression
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 01 September 2026;
tldr: Proposes a single-operation Rydberg phase gate using dynamic population suppression to improve fidelity in neutral-atom quantum computing.
motivation: Neutral-atom platforms with Rydberg interactions are promising for quantum computing, but fast and high-fidelity two-qubit gates remain challenging due to unwanted population in Rydberg states.
method: The scheme employs laser control and Rydberg blockade to dynamically suppress population in the Rydberg state, enabling a phase gate in a single operation.
result: The approach achieves a single-step Rydberg phase gate with potentially reduced errors and simpler experimental requirements compared to multi-pulse protocols.
conclusion: Dynamic population suppression offers a practical route toward high-fidelity Rydberg phase gates for neutral-atom quantum processors.

title: Criteria For Unbiased Estimation: Applications To Noise-agnostic Sensing And Quantum Channel Estimation
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 14 September 2026;
tldr: The paper establishes criteria for unbiased estimation in quantum settings, with applications to noise-agnostic sensing and quantum channel estimation.
motivation: Unbiased estimation is essential for accurate quantum parameter estimation, but noise and channel imperfections often prevent unbiasedness; general criteria are needed to guide protocol design.
method: The authors derive theoretical criteria for the existence of unbiased estimators in quantum estimation problems and apply them to noise-agnostic sensing and quantum channel estimation scenarios.
result: The criteria identify conditions under which unbiased estimation is possible and yield concrete protocols for noise-agnostic sensing and quantum channel estimation.
conclusion: This work provides a foundation for designing unbiased quantum estimation protocols that are robust to noise and applicable to channel characterization.

title: Satellite-to-ground Quantum Key Distribution Model Under Time-evolving Turbulence
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 09 September 2026;
tldr: The paper develops a satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution model that accounts for time-evolving atmospheric turbulence.
motivation: Satellite-based QKD is a key step toward global quantum networks, but atmospheric turbulence and its temporal variation can severely degrade channel performance, requiring accurate and dynamic channel models.
method: The authors construct a theoretical model for the satellite-to-ground QKD channel where turbulence statistics evolve over time, likely using simulation and analysis of key rate under time-dependent atmospheric conditions.
result: The model captures the impact of time-evolving turbulence on QKD performance, providing a more realistic assessment of key generation rates and channel loss for satellite links.
conclusion: This work offers a practical modeling framework for evaluating and designing satellite-to-ground QKD systems under realistic, dynamically changing atmospheric conditions.

title: Quantum Coulomb Drag Signatures Of Majorana Bound States
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 15 September 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes Coulomb drag as a transport signature for detecting Majorana bound states in hybrid quantum devices.
motivation: Majorana bound states are central to topological quantum computing, but their unambiguous detection remains experimentally challenging.
method: The authors theoretically analyze Coulomb drag in systems hosting Majorana bound states, likely using linear response and Green's function techniques.
result: They identify characteristic Coulomb drag signatures that can distinguish Majorana bound states from trivial Andreev states or other quasiparticles.
conclusion: Coulomb drag measurements may serve as a practical diagnostic for Majorana bound states, aiding the development of topological qubit platforms.

title: Security Risks Of VOA-induced Luminescence In Chip-based Quantum Key Distribution
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 09 September 2026;
tldr: This paper identifies and analyzes security vulnerabilities caused by VOA-induced luminescence in chip-based quantum key distribution systems.
motivation: Chip-based QKD is a promising route to practical quantum networks, but hardware imperfections such as unintended light emission from variable optical attenuators can open side channels that compromise security.
method: The authors experimentally characterize the luminescence of VOAs, demonstrate an attack that exploits this side channel, and propose countermeasures to mitigate the vulnerability.

title: Theoretical Guarantees Of Variational Quantum Algorithm With Guiding States
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 01 September 2026;
tldr: This paper establishes theoretical guarantees for variational quantum algorithms augmented with guiding states.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms are widely used for near-term quantum devices, but rigorous performance guarantees are often lacking.
method: The authors analyze the optimization and convergence properties of VQAs when a guiding state is incorporated, using mathematical bounds or conditions.
result: They derive conditions under which guiding states improve the reliability and convergence of variational quantum algorithms.
conclusion: Guiding states can provide theoretical assurances for VQAs, though the approach remains outside the core interests of quantum information theory.
